SAN JOSE, Calif., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Semiconductor Industry Association (SIA) today announced that Cirrus Logic (NASDAQ: CRUS) President and CEO John Forsyth has been elected Chair of the SIA Board of Directors. Tom Caulfield, Executive Chairman of GlobalFoundries (NASDAQ: GFS), was elected Vice Chair. AMD (NASDAQ: AMD) Chair and CEO Lisa Su, who served as 2026 Chair, will continue to serve on the Board and the Leadership Committee. SIA, the voice of the semiconductor industry, represents 99% of the U.S. semiconductor industry by revenue and nearly two-thirds of non-U.S. chip firms.

"Congratulations to John Forsyth on his election as SIA Chair. John has been a trusted partner since my first day at SIA, and he brings steady, strategic judgment to a pivotal year for our industry," said SIA President and CEO Michael Robbins. "With a new Congress, SIA's 50th anniversary, and the work of extending the Advanced Manufacturing Investment Credit ahead of us, I look forward to working with John, Tom Caulfield, and our entire Board to strengthen America's semiconductor leadership. I also want to thank Lisa Su for an outstanding year as our Chair. Her steadfast leadership strengthens SIA and our industry, and I am tremendously grateful for her guidance and counsel."

Forsyth brings more than 20 years of experience in semiconductor industry leadership. As president and CEO of Cirrus Logic, he leads the company in developing high-precision, low-power audio and mixed-signal semiconductor solutions for a broad range of consumer, automotive, and industrial applications. Forsyth has served as president and chief executive officer of Cirrus Logic since January 2021. He joined the company in 2014 through its acquisition of Wolfson Microelectronics and was named president in 2020 after previous roles including chief strategy officer and vice president of marketing.

"I'm honored to serve as SIA Chair at such an important time for our industry," said John Forsyth, president and CEO of Cirrus Logic. "America's leadership in the next wave of semiconductor innovation depends on both a thriving domestic industry and close collaboration between that industry and government. I look forward to working with SIA's Board of Directors and members to strengthen that collaboration, accelerate the build-out of a more resilient domestic supply chain, and keep the U.S. at the forefront of this critical technology."

About SIA
The Semiconductor Industry Association (SIA) is the voice of the semiconductor industry, one of America's top export industries and a key driver of America's economic strength, national security, and global competitiveness. SIA represents 99% of the U.S. semiconductor industry by revenue and nearly two-thirds of non-U.S. chip firms. Through this coalition, SIA seeks to strengthen leadership of semiconductor manufacturing, design, and research by working with Congress, the Administration, and key industry stakeholders around the world to encourage policies that fuel innovation, propel business, and drive international competition. Learn more at semiconductors.org.

HOUSTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Geospace Technologies Corporation (NASDAQ: GEOS) (“the “Company") today reported revenue for the fourth quarter ended September 30, 2026, of $19.6 million compared to revenue of $30.7 million for the comparable year-ago period. Net loss for the fourth quarter ended September 30, 2026 was $13.7 million, or $(1.06) per basic and diluted share, compared to a net loss of $9.1 million, or $(0.71) per basic and diluted share, for the comparable year-ago period. The fourth quarter loss included non-cash charges of $3.5 million cumulative translation loss related to the Company’s Colombian operations and $2.9 million for underutilized assets related to select nodal rental tools and manufacturing equipment.

For the twelve-month period ended September 30, 2026, Geospace Technologies reported revenue of $80.7 million for its fiscal year ended September 30, 2026. This compares to revenue of $110.8 million for the comparable year-ago period. Net loss for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2026 was $44.3 million, or $(3.43) basic and per diluted share, compared to a net loss of $9.7 million, or $(0.76) per basic and diluted share, for comparable year-ago period.

Management’s Comments

Richard “Rich” Kelley, Chief Executive Officer and President of Geospace Technologies, said, “To provide an understanding of our financial performance this fiscal year, it is beneficial to consider the global economic picture. The year remained plagued by uncertainty and delays driven by ongoing changes in trade policy, a major Middle East energy disruption, continued sanctions, and shifts in borrowing costs. These significant factors negatively impacted our ability to conduct business in our current structure.

As such, the management team has taken decisive steps to realign our operations, reduce costs, and position Geospace for a return to profitability. During fiscal year 2026, we have executed two reductions in force, an early retirement program, and cutbacks in expenses. Additionally, the challenging business conditions during fiscal 2026 contributed to non-cash charges recorded for the fiscal year of approximately $6 million of cumulative foreign exchange loss and underutilized equipment.

Our Smart Water segment experienced disappointing declines driven predominantly by decreases in orders for our Hydroconn line of smart water meter connector cables. Evaluation of broader market conditions point to slower hardware shipments, uneven project deployments, and normalization following earlier demand surges. Several major metering suppliers are experiencing near-term hardware and deployment softness, while longer-term modernization demand appears more resilient. As part of our business restructuring, we concluded a decades long relationship with an external manufacturing representative firm, who exclusively marketed the Hydroconn connectors. In fiscal year 2027, we will use internal sales and marketing resources to build demand and secure specifications of our products in utility AMI-related procurements. This approach will reduce expenses associated with representative commissions and increase our control over product promotion and increase customer intimacy. While the contribution from the Aquana brand remains modest, the products continue to grow with 51% year over year revenue increases. In the coming year, we look to build upon the growth in Aquana revenue and maximize our early efforts with white label product manufacturing to support a revenue rebound in this segment.

Our Energy Solutions segment experienced the impacts of energy market volatility and project timing shifts, increased component and shipping costs, as well as access to raw materials. Increased competition and consolidation remain challenging in the marine exploration market and have led to decreased demand for our ocean-bottom nodes. The segment focused resources on execution of sizable contracts including the Petrobras Permanent Reservoir Monitoring (PRM) program, which is expected to be shipped and product-related revenue recognized by the end of fiscal year 2027. The previously cited global conditions proved harshest for our energy sales efforts, however, we have a strong backlog in this segment going into the next fiscal year. Long-term demand forecasts should drive more favorable land exploration market conditions resulting in additional Pioneer contracts.

For the Intelligent Industrial segment, the economic headwinds were less severe but still influenced revenue timing. The biggest factor impacting revenue generation was government procurement timing at state and federal levels. After a lengthy effort, our Quantum Technology Sciences subsidiary entered into a $10.8 million contract with the U.S. Naval Surface Warfare Center Crane Division, Crane, Indiana for the Company’s Seismic Acoustic Detection and Ranging Underwater System. Similar timing delays have occurred around the sale of the Heartbeat Detector®, a vehicle security screening technology used by correctional and border agencies. Lengthy procurement cycles and complex approvals have resulted in slower than expected revenue recognition with this product line, but the outlook and demand for the technology remain extremely encouraging.

Despite this incredibly challenging year, our restructuring decisions and implementation will set the company more solidly on a return to profitability in fiscal year 2027. We concluded fiscal year 2026 with a backlog exceeding $100 million from contracts across our three segments. Contributions to the backlog encompass not only the PRM program, but contracts with the U.S. Federal government and other agencies as well as contract manufacturing customers and smart water white label commitments. The strong backlog, a well targeted acquisition strategy and restructured operations prepare Geospace well for the future.”

Smart Water Segment

Revenue from the Company’s Smart Water segment totaled $3.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026. This compares to $8.5 million in revenue for the same period a year ago a decrease of 63%. For the fiscal year, revenue from this segment totaled $17.2 million versus $35.8 million for the same prior year period for a decrease of 52%. The decrease in revenue for the three-month and twelve-month periods is due to decreased demand for our Hydroconn universal AMI connectors.

Energy Solutions Segment

For the three-month period ended September 30, 2026, revenue from the Company’s Energy Solutions segment totaled $10.8 million for a decrease of 31% when compared to $15.7 million from the same prior year period. Revenue from the twelve-month period was $40.9 million, a decrease of 19%, when compared to revenue from the same prior year period of $50.7 million. The decrease for the three-month period and twelve-month period is due to lower utilization and sales for our marine ocean bottom node rental fleet, partially offset by revenue recognized related to performance on our PRM contract and sales of the Company’s ultralight land node known as Pioneer.

Intelligent Industrial Segment

Revenue from the Company’s Intelligent Industrial segment totaled $5.6 million for the three-month period ended September 30, 2026. This compares with $6.4 million from the equivalent year ago period, representing a decrease of 12%. Revenue for the twelve-month period ending September 30, 2026, was $22.2 million. This compares to the prior year-ago period of $24.0 million, a decrease of 7%. The decrease in revenue for the three-month period and twelve-month period was due to lower demand for our industrial sensors, and imaging products, partially offset by an increase in security and defense revenue.

Balance Sheet and Liquidity

For the twelve-month period ended September 30, 2026, the Company used $35.1 million in cash and cash equivalents from operating activities. The Company generated $9.8 million of cash from investing activities that included $12.1 million of proceeds from the sale of rental equipment, $1.4 million in proceeds from the sale of property, plant and equipment and, offset by $3.9 million for additions to property, plant and equipment. The Company generated $7.1 million of cash from financing activities of which $7.5 million was from borrowings from the Company’s Woodforest credit facility.

On October 29, 2026, the Company entered into a Revolving Loan and Security Agreement with Amerisource Funding, Inc. (the "Amerisource Agreement"). The Company had a $7.5 million outstanding loan balance under the Woodforest Agreement, which was refinanced with borrowings under the Amerisource Agreement at closing. The Amerisource Agreement is for a three-year term and provides a revolving credit facility with a maximum availability of $25 million, subject to a borrowing base. Interest shall accrue on outstanding borrowings at the prime rate plus 3.5% per annum. The Company is required to make monthly interest payments on borrowed funds. The Amerisource Agreement is secured by substantially all of the Company’s assets, except for certain excluded property, and is guaranteed by certain of the Company’s subsidiaries. As of the date of this announcement, the Company has available borrowings of approximately $13 million.

Conference Call Information

Geospace Technologies will host a conference call to review its fourth quarter and fiscal year 2026 financial results on Friday, November 20, 2026, at 10:00 a.m. Eastern Time (9 a.m. Central). Participants can access the call at 833-316-1983 (US) or 785-838-9310 (International). Please reference the conference ID: GEOSQ426 prior to the start of the conference call. A replay will be available for approximately 60 days and may be accessed through the Investor Relations page of our website at www.geospace.com.

About Geospace Technologies

Geospace Technologies is a global technology and instrumentation manufacturer specializing in advanced sensing, IOT and highly ruggedized products, which serve smart water, energy exploration, industrial, government and commercial customers worldwide. The Company’s products blend engineering expertise with advanced analytic software to optimize energy exploration, enhance national and homeland security, empower water utility and property managers, and streamline electronic printing solutions. With more than four decades of excellence, the Company’s 390 employees across the world are dedicated to engineering and technical quality. Geospace is traded on the U.S. NASDAQ stock exchange under the ticker symbol GEOS. For more information, visit www.geospace.com.

Key Terms

cumulative translation lossfinancial
The accumulated change in value that arises when a company translates the financial statements of its foreign operations into the reporting (presentation) currency; exchange-rate movements create periodic translation gains or losses that are recorded each period and summed as the cumulative translation loss. It is a non-cash accounting adjustment that typically appears in equity (as part of accumulated other comprehensive income or loss) rather than in operating profit, and the accumulated amount may be reclassified into profit or loss if the foreign operation is sold or substantially liquidated.
permanent reservoir monitoringtechnical
Permanent reservoir monitoring is the long-term use of sensors and measurement systems placed at or near an underground oil, gas or fluid reservoir to continuously track pressure, temperature, flow and small seismic changes. For investors it matters because continuous, real-time data reduces uncertainty about how much can be recovered, helps operators optimize production and costs, and lowers environmental and operational risk — like putting the asset on a continuous health monitor to inform valuation and investment decisions.
revolving credit facilityfinancial
A revolving credit facility is a type of loan that a business can borrow from whenever it needs money, up to a set limit. It’s like having a credit card for companies—allowing them to borrow, pay back, and borrow again as needed, providing flexibility for managing cash flow or funding short-term expenses.
borrowing basefinancial
A borrowing base is the amount a lender will allow a company to borrow based on the value of assets the company offers as security, typically things like accounts receivable and inventory. It matters to investors because it sets a practical ceiling on short-term financing and influences a company’s liquidity and risk: if the borrowing base falls, the company may lose access to cash or be forced to sell assets, which can affect operations and share value.

SALT LAKE CITY, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Co-Diagnostics, Inc. (Nasdaq: CODX) ("Co-Diagnostics" or "the Company"), a molecular diagnostics company with a unique, patented platform for the development of molecular diagnostic tests, today announced that it has filed Articles of Amendment to its Articles of Incorporation (the "Amendment") to effect a reverse stock split of its issued and outstanding common stock at a ratio of 1-for-25 shares (the "Reverse Stock Split"). The Reverse Stock Split will become effective at 12:01 a.m. ET on Tuesday, November 24, 2026. The Company's common stock will continue to trade on The Nasdaq Capital Market under the symbol "CODX" and will begin trading on a split-adjusted basis when the market opens on Tuesday, November 24, 2026. The Reverse Stock Split is intended to enable the Company to maintain compliance with the $1.00 minimum bid price requirement for continued listing on The Nasdaq Capital Market, and to maintain sufficient authorized shares available for issuance to allow the Company to conduct equity financings as needed. The new CUSIP number for the Company's common stock following the Reverse Stock Split will be 189763 303.

At the Special Meeting of Stockholders held on November 13, 2026 (the "Special Meeting"), the Company's stockholders approved an amendment to the Company's Articles of Incorporation, as amended, to effect one or more reverse stock splits of the Company's issued and outstanding shares of common stock, on one or more occasions, at a ratio of not less than 1-for-2, with the cumulative effect of all such reverse stock splits not to exceed 1-for-750, such final ratio or ratios and the timing and number of any reverse stock splits to be determined by the Company's board of directors at any time within twelve months following the Special Meeting, without further approval or authorization of the stockholders. Additional information regarding the Reverse Stock Split approved by stockholders can be found in the Company's definitive proxy statement filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC") on October 26, 2026.

The Amendment provides that at the effective time of the Reverse Stock Split, each 25 shares of the Company's issued and outstanding common stock will be automatically combined into one (1) validly issued, fully paid and non-assessable share of common stock, without effecting a change to the par value per share. The Reverse Stock Split will impact all shares of the Company's common stock outstanding immediately prior to the effective time of the Reverse Stock Split, as well as the number of shares of common stock available for issuance under the Company's equity incentive plans. In addition, the Reverse Stock Split will effect a reduction in the number of shares of common stock issuable upon the exercise of stock options and warrants outstanding immediately prior to the effectiveness of the Reverse Stock Split with a corresponding increase in the applicable exercise price per share, in each case in accordance with the terms thereof. The Reverse Stock Split will not change the number of shares of capital stock authorized for issuance under our Articles of Incorporation. Based on the 13,044,465 shares of common stock currently outstanding, we expect approximately 521,779 shares of common stock to be issued and outstanding following the Reverse Stock Split.

No fractional shares will be issued in connection with the Reverse Stock Split. Stockholders who would otherwise be entitled to receive fractional shares as a result of the Reverse Stock Split will have those shares rounded up to the next whole share. Stockholders with shares in brokerage accounts should direct any questions concerning the reverse stock split to their broker; all other stockholders may direct questions to the Company's transfer agent, VStock Transfer, LLC.

About Co-Diagnostics, Inc.:

Co-Diagnostics, Inc., a Utah corporation, is a molecular diagnostics company that develops, manufactures and markets state-of-the-art diagnostics technologies. The Company's technologies are utilized for tests that are designed using the detection and/or analysis of nucleic acid molecules (DNA or RNA). The Company also uses its proprietary technology to design specific tests for its Co-Dx PCR at-home and point-of-care platform (subject to regulatory review and not currently for sale) and to identify genetic markers for use in applications other than infectious disease.

Melville, New York--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - As previously disclosed, on December 23, 2025, FONAR Corporation (NASDAQ: FONR) ("FONAR" or the "Company") entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger (the "Merger Agreement") with FONAR, LLC ("Parent") and Fonar Acquisition Sub, Inc. ("Merger Sub"), pursuant to which, subject to the satisfaction of the conditions set forth in the Merger Agreement, Parent would acquire the Company in an all-cash merger (the "Merger"). Under Section 3.22(a) of the Merger Agreement, the Merger was conditioned on (a) the affirmative vote of shares representing a majority of the stock outstanding and entitled to vote, voting together as a single class, after giving effect to the respective voting powers of each class of stock, and (b) the affirmative vote of a majority of the votes cast by disinterested stockholders, voting together as a single class after giving effect to the respective voting powers of each class of stock.

On February 2, 2026, plaintiff Bruce Taylor ("Plaintiff"), a purported stockholder of the Company, filed a Verified Stockholder Class Action Complaint (the "Complaint"), on behalf of himself and all other similarly situated stockholders of the Company, in the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware (the "Court"), captioned Taylor v. Fonar Corporation, et al., C.A. No. 2026-0142-JTL (the "Action"). The Complaint named as defendants the Company, Parent, Merger Sub, and Timothy Damadian, Luciano Bonanni, Robert M. Carrino, Ronald G. Lehman, and Richard E. Turk (the "Individual Defendants" and, together with the Company, Parent, and Merger Sub, the "Defendants").

The Complaint alleged that, under Section 203 of the Delaware General Corporation Law ("Section 203"), the Merger must be conditioned on the affirmative vote of at least 66⅔% of the outstanding voting stock of the Company which is not owned by an interested stockholder, as provided in Section 203(a)(3) (the "Section 203 Vote"). The Complaint further alleged that the Individual Defendants breached their fiduciary duties in connection with the foregoing.

Defendants have denied, and continue to deny, that they committed any violation of law or engaged in any of the wrongful acts that were or could have been alleged in the Action, and expressly maintain that they complied with their fiduciary and other legal duties.

On May 29, 2026, the Company filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC") a Current Report on Form 8-K calculating the Section 203 Vote, and the Company received approval of the requisite 66⅔% of the outstanding voting stock of the Company which is not owned by an interested stockholder under Section 203(a)(3) (the "Section 203 Approval").

On June 5, 2026, the Court granted and approved a stipulation and order voluntarily dismissing the Action as moot (the "Dismissal Order"). The Dismissal Order dismissed all claims in the Action with prejudice only as to Plaintiff and without prejudice as to any actual or potential claims of any other members of the putative class, and the Court retained jurisdiction to determine Plaintiff's application for an award of attorneys' fees and expenses (the "Fee and Expense Application"). The Dismissal Order was without prejudice to Plaintiff's ability to subsequently file claims challenging the fairness of the Merger and/or the adequacy of the Company's disclosures in connection with the Merger on any basis other than the adequacy of the Company's disclosures regarding Section 203, and Defendants reserved all rights with respect to any such claims.

Following arm's-length negotiations, the parties to the Action agreed to fully resolve the Fee and Expense Application through a payment to Plaintiff's counsel, which the Company will make and/or cause to be made on behalf of all Defendants, in the amount of $1,600,000 (the "Mootness Fee"). The Company, while denying any and all liability, agreed to the Mootness Fee in the exercise of its business judgment in order to avoid the cost, distraction, and uncertainty of further litigation regarding the Fee and Expense Application. The Court has not been asked to review and will not pass judgment on the payment of the Mootness Fee.

On November 15, 2026, the Court entered a Stipulation and Order Governing Plaintiff's Counsel's Award of Attorneys' Fees and Expenses, Notice of Mootness Fee and Closing the Action (the "Fee Order"). Pursuant to the Fee Order, within thirty (30) calendar days of the later of (i) the Court's entry of the Fee Order or (ii) the provision by Plaintiff's counsel of a Form W-9 and wiring instructions to the Company, the Company will pay or cause to be paid the Mootness Fee to Plaintiff's counsel in full and complete satisfaction of the Fee and Expense Application in connection with the Action. Upon receipt of such payment, Plaintiff and Plaintiff's counsel will be deemed to have fully and completely released all Defendants, and each of their respective subsidiaries, affiliates, parents, divisions, directors, officers, employees, predecessors and successors, managers, equity holders, beneficiaries, members, any related persons or entities, insurers, trustees, administrators, representatives and fiduciaries, successors, assigns and agents, from all claims for attorneys' fees and expenses in connection with the Action.

This Notice is being disseminated pursuant to the Fee Order and constitutes notice to the Company's stockholders, including the members of the putative class, to the extent required under Court of Chancery Rule 23. Pursuant to the Fee Order, within five (5) business days of the dissemination of this notice, the Company will file an affidavit with the Court confirming its compliance with the Fee Order's notice requirement, upon which the Register in Chancery is directed to close the Action on the docket for all purposes.

Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Tenet Fintech Group Inc. (CSE: PKK) (OTCQB: PKKFF) (FSE: P0T) ("Tenet" or the "Company"), an innovative analytics service provider, owner and operator of the Cubeler Business Hub, today announced its financial results and operating highlights for the three-month and nine-month periods ended September 30, 2026. Tenet reported revenue of $66,070,573 for the quarter, compared to $192,769 in the third quarter of 2025, and a net profit of $1,593,915 for the third quarter of 2026, compared to a net loss of $3,594,470 in the third quarter of 2025. All amounts in this news release are in Canadian dollars unless otherwise indicated.

Q3-2026 Key Financial Figures

  • Total Revenue of $66.07 million

  • Net Profit of $1.59 million

Q3-2026 Operating Highlights

The Company's value-added services to China's real estate development and construction sector supply chains through its GoldRiver and Cubeler Business Hub platforms continued to drive revenue in the third quarter of 2026 and provided a solid foundation to build on. Tenet's November 2025 breakthrough framework agreement with Chengdu Honglongyi Trading Ltd. ("CHTL") was the catalyst for much of the activity on the Company's platforms through the first three quarters of 2026. For most of the first half of 2026, CHTL was the sole customer driving meaningful supply-chain-related activity on the Company's platforms. To reduce its dependency on a single customer, the Company made increasing the number of its supply-chain customers a priority. The Company added five new customers between the latter part of the second quarter and the end of the third quarter, bringing the number of customers that contributed to its supply-chain-related revenue during the third quarter to a total of six, including CHTL.

Tenet officially ceased its operations in China's small-business commercial-lending space by selling its 51% ownership stake in its Asia Synergy Financial Capital ("ASFC") subsidiary during the third quarter of 2026. The transaction aligns with the Company's stated desire to focus its operations in China on data aggregation and supply-chain-related activities. The sale of ASFC not only frees up valuable resources but is expected to provide significant capital that can be allocated to bolster the Company's supply-chain-related activities and data-related service offerings in both China and North America.

Although the Company was still not at the commercialization phase during the third quarter of 2026 when it comes to its data-derived product offering, the Company believes that relevant progress was made toward achieving that objective. Tenet made several enhancements to the Cubeler Business Hub, including the addition of a grant-matching feature for registered members, to make the platform more enticing for SMEs. The Company also enhanced its offering to accountants and bookkeepers with the launch of its BKeeper platform allowing them to offer their SME clients with a host of AI-powered value-added services. Those initiatives, combined with the arrival of a new sales manager, contributed to a noticeable increase in the rate of SME registrations on the Cubeler Business Hub during the quarter. With the increase in the amount of SME data at its disposal during the quarter, the Company was optimistic that the launch of a commercially viable series of Canadian economic indexes could be achieved in relatively short order.

Q3-2026 Financial Results Summary

The Company's reported net income in Q3 was significantly impacted by certain nonrecurring events during the quarter. Those events include: 1) the profit realized on the sale of the Company's ASFC financial services subsidiary; 2) the commission paid related to the $225M minimum guaranteed annual revenue agreement signed with Sum Hung Hang Tai Trading Ltd.; 3) the grant of stock options to directors, officers, employees and consultants; 4) an increase in expected credit loss provision related to prepayments made to certain subcontractors dating back to 2022; and 5) the impairment of intangible assets related to ASFC. Together, these five events accounted for net expenses of a little more than $1.7M for the Company in the third quarter, which explains the lower net income reported for the quarter compared to the previous quarter, despite the quarter-over-quarter revenue increase from Q2-2026 to Q3-2026.

In summary, the Company generated revenue of $66,070,573 for the three-month period and $129,443,140 for the nine-month period ended September 30, 2026, compared to $192,769 for the three-month period and $736,677 for the nine-month period ended September 30, 2025.

Total expenses before taxes for the quarter amounted to $63,406,975 compared to $3,702,406 for the same period in 2025. The Company realized a net profit of $1,593,915 for the three-month period and $4,984,526 for the nine-month period ended September 30, 2026, compared to a net loss of $3,594,470 for the three-month period and a net loss of $9,156,663 for the nine-month period ended September 30, 2025.

Full details of the Company's third quarter 2026 financial results can be found in the Unaudited Condensed Interim Consolidated Financial Statements and Management's Discussion and Analysis (MD&A) for the three-month and nine-month periods ended September 30, 2026, and September 30, 2025, which are available under the Company's profile at www.sedarplus.com.

Revised Full-Year 2026 Revenue Guidance

Tenet's strong third-quarter results, coupled with the addition of new clients for its supply-chain-related service offerings, led the Company to revise its full-year 2026 revenue guidance range to between $190 million and $195 million (up from $175 million to $180 million). Tenet expects gross profit margins of 9% to 11% and net income of $9.8 million to $10.5 million. The revised numbers should only marginally affect Tenet's previously forecasted EPS, which the Company has kept at $0.02 to $0.025 for fiscal year 2026.

Q3-2026 Results Q&A and Full-Year Outlook for 2026

Tenet CEO Johnson Joseph will answer shareholder questions about the Company's Q3-2026 financial results in a Q&A interview and share his perspective on the Company's business plan for the rest of 2026. Shareholders are invited to read the Company's MD&A prior to sending their questions related to these subjects to the Company. Questions received by 9:00 pm EST on November 24, 2026, sent to the Company's investor relations mailbox at investors@tenetfintech.com or sent to cathy@chfir.com will be answered to the extent that they can be answered in compliance with Canadian securities regulations. The Company will post the Q&A interview on its website by 5:00 pm EST on November 27, 2026.

SAN DIEGO, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- For customers, electric reliability is measured in everyday moments: whether the lights come on in the morning, a business can keep its doors open and power is restored quickly when an outage occurs. For the 21st consecutive year, San Diego Gas & Electric (SDG&E), a subsidiary of Sempra (NYSE: SRE), has been recognized as the most reliable electric utility in the West. PA Consulting presented SDG&E with the 2026 ReliabilityOne® Award for Outstanding Reliability Performance in the Western region.

Over the past decade, the average SDG&E customer has experienced fewer than one sustained outage a year, while the average amount of time without power from unplanned outages has remained at approximately 70 minutes annually. Momentary interruptions have declined 18% since 2016. In 2025, outage frequency and duration, excluding major event days, were at their lowest levels since 2017.

The results reflect long-term investment in a modern grid, predictive tools that help identify problems earlier and smart-grid technology that can isolate an issue and limit the number of customers affected.

"As we work to improve affordability and deliver energy at the lowest cost possible, safety and reliability will always remain the focus at SDG&E," said Scott Crider, president of SDG&E. "Our customers depend on us to ensure power is there when it's needed most. I'm proud of our employees who work every day to deliver on this commitment and have helped make SDG&E the most reliable utility in the West for 21 years."

Delivering reliable energy around the clock takes more than technology. It takes a skilled local workforce, a resilient supply chain and trusted contractor partnerships. SDG&E's crews live and work in the communities they serve, and they're on call around the clock to maintain the system and restore power quickly. Suppliers and contractors back them up by delivering critical materials when they're needed. Together, they help prevent outages, respond when problems occur and restore power as safely and quickly as possible.

Delivering Reliability More Affordably 
SDG&E also considers cost and efficiency when making the investments that support reliable service. The same technology behind 21 years of top reliability performance, from smart switches that limit outages to AI that helps spot risks sooner, can help the company operate more efficiently and address potential problems before they become larger, more costly repairs.

What 21 Years of Reliability Means for Customers
SDG&E's reliability record rests on investments in people, infrastructure and technology designed to identify risks earlier, limit outages and restore power faster for the 3.6 million people it serves.

  • Seeing Risk Sooner: SDG&E launched Edge Alert Sentinel (EAS), an edge AI collaboration with Qualcomm Technologies and UC San Diego's Scripps Institution of Oceanography. EAS builds on a network of high-definition cameras and artificial intelligence to support early fire detection. It also works alongside advanced sectionalizing devices that automatically isolate problems on the grid. For customers, that means risks are spotted earlier and fewer homes lose power.
  • A Stronger Grid and Faster Restoration: SDG&E replaced older underground cables and overhead lines, added smart switches that help limit outages, and improved restoration processes to restore power faster. Modernized data systems help teams make quicker decisions and learn from every outage. For customers, that means fewer interruptions, shorter outages, real-time outage updates and an easy-to-use online outage tracking tool.
  • A Culture of Safety: SDG&E was California's first utility to earn Cal/OSHA's elite Voluntary Protection Program safety certification for one of its facilities, exceeding industry standards for operational excellence. For customers, that means a well-trained workforce that keeps safety first while keeping the energy system running.

Independent Oversight, Local Accountability
SDG&E's investments are reviewed by the California Public Utilities Commission through an independent, public process. That oversight helps make sure the work that keeps San Diego's grid among the most reliable in the nation is focused, disciplined and transparent.

"Utilities such as SDG&E are committed to delivering reliable service, enhancing resiliency, and maintaining affordability for their customers," said PA's ReliabilityOne® Program Director Patrick Graves. "Increasingly, technology is being used to augment existing capabilities and improve overall system efficiency. These advancements include more accurate estimated restoration times, the implementation of advanced control systems that allow operators to manage infrastructure through a single user interface, and the integration of hardware and software to streamline restoration efforts. At the same time, utilities are continuing to refine and leverage technology to keep rates affordable and accessible for all customers. At PA, we're proud to be working with utilities that are embracing this kind of innovation to meet evolving customer expectations."

All utilities operating electric delivery systems in North America are eligible for consideration for the ReliabilityOne® Award. This year PA recognized six leading utilities in their respective regions, which include utilities from the Northeast, Mid-Atlantic, Midwest, Upper Midwest, Southeast and Pacific Regions. The selection of provisional recipients is based primarily on system reliability statistics that measure the frequency (SAIFI) and duration of customer outages (SAIDI and CAIDI). After provisional recipients are selected, each company undergoes a rigorous certification process, which provides an independent review and confirmation of the policies, processes and systems used to collect, analyze and report a company's reliability results. Additional awards are recognized based on analysis of certification findings.

To learn more about SDG&E and its initiatives, visit SDGEtoday.com.

About PA Consulting
PA Consulting believes in the power of ingenuity to build a positive human future. As strategies, technologies and innovation collide, we create opportunity from complexity. Our diverse teams combine deep expertise, innovative thinking and breakthrough technologies to help clients adapt, transform and achieve enduring results across consumer and manufacturing, defense and security, energy and utilities, financial services, government and public services, health and life sciences and transport. As a Jacobs company, we combine strategic advisory, design and delivery as a single partner across the full program lifecycle. Together, our global team of approximately 47,000 helps clients shape investment decisions, solve complex challenges and deliver lasting outcomes. Discover more at paconsulting.com and connect with PA on LinkedIn. PA. Bringing Ingenuity to Life.

PA Consulting's ReliabilityOne® Awards are presented to electric utilities providing their customers with the highest levels of reliability in the industry. PA Consulting's ReliabilityOne® study is based on standard industry reliability statistics that measure the frequency and duration of electric power outages. As a group, customers of ReliabilityOne® participants on average experienced over 56% fewer sustained outages, and their collective system saw 64% shorter outage durations than the average US investor-owned utility. PA Consulting has been analyzing electric utility performance since 1987. For more information about PA Consulting, visit https://www.paconsulting.com/industries/energyand-utilities.

About SDG&E
San Diego Gas & Electric (SDG&E) is an innovative energy-delivery company that provides clean, safe and reliable energy to better the lives of the people it serves across 27 cities and two counties in the San Diego and southern Orange County region. SDG&E is a recognized leader in its industry and community, as demonstrated by being named Corporate Partner of the Year at the San Diego Business Journal's Nonprofit & Corporate Citizenship Awards and receiving PA Consulting's ReliabilityOne® Award for Outstanding Reliability Performance for 21 consecutive years. SDG&E is a subsidiary of Sempra (NYSE: SRE), a leading U.S. utility growth business. For more information, visit SDGEtoday.com or connect with SDG&E on social media @SDGE.

DALLAS--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Energy Transfer LP (TXSE: ET) has completed its previously announced acquisition of Vaquero Midstream LLC. Total consideration for the transaction was $1.95 billion in cash and approximately 33.3 million newly issued Energy Transfer common units.

The acquired assets add the Caymus Processing Complex, which includes three processing trains with a total capacity of approximately 675 MMcf/d and approximately 300 miles of pipeline serving leading operators across some of the most active areas of the Delaware Basin.

The transaction is expected to further strengthen Energy Transfer's Permian footprint by increasing access to growing natural gas and NGL production volumes while enhancing connectivity to the Partnership's broader midstream platform.

Energy Transfer LP (TXSE: ET) owns and operates one of the largest and most diversified portfolios of energy assets in the United States, with approximately 140,000 miles of pipeline and associated energy infrastructure. Energy Transfer’s strategic network spans 44 states with assets in all of the major U.S. production basins. Energy Transfer is a publicly traded limited partnership with core operations that include complementary natural gas midstream, intrastate and interstate transportation and storage assets; crude oil, natural gas liquids (“NGL”) and refined product transportation and terminalling assets; and NGL fractionation. Energy Transfer also owns the general partner interests, the incentive distribution rights and approximately 28 million common units (representing 15% of the aggregate outstanding common units and Class D units) of Sunoco LP (TXSE: SUN), the managing member interests in SunocoCorp LLC (TXSE: SUNC), and the general partner interests and approximately 46 million common units (representing 32% of the outstanding common units) of USA Compression Partners, LP (TXSE: USAC). For more information, visit the Energy Transfer LP website at www.energytransfer.com.

Sunoco LP (TXSE: SUN) is a leading energy infrastructure and fuel distribution master limited partnership operating across 33 countries and territories in North America, the Greater Caribbean, and Europe. SUN's midstream operations include an extensive network of approximately 14,000 miles of pipeline and over 170 terminals. This critical infrastructure complements SUN's fuel distribution operations which distribute over 17 billion gallons annually to approximately 11,000 Sunoco and partner-branded retail locations, as well as independent dealers and commercial customers. SUN's general partner is owned by Energy Transfer LP. For more information, visit the Sunoco LP website at www.sunocolp.com.

SunocoCorp LLC (TXSE: SUNC) is a publicly traded limited liability company that owns a direct limited partner interest in Sunoco LP. For more information, visit the Sunoco LP website at www.sunocolp.com.

USA Compression Partners, LP (TXSE: USAC) is one of the nation’s largest independent providers of natural gas compression services in terms of total compression fleet horsepower. USAC partners with a broad customer base composed of producers, processors, gatherers, and transporters of natural gas and crude oil. USAC focuses on providing midstream natural gas compression services to infrastructure applications primarily in high-volume gathering systems, processing facilities, and transportation applications. Regional reliability and grid flexibility work also recognized with additional awards

CHICAGO--(BUSINESS WIRE)--ComEd customers are served by the most reliable electric utility in the nation. PA Consulting yesterday presented ComEd with its 2026 ReliabilityOne® National Reliability Award, Outstanding Reliability Performance in the Midwest Region and the Grid Flexibility Awards. ComEd previously won the award in 2023.

"Being named the most reliable electric utility in the country is a credit to the dedication of our ComEd workforce and a demonstration of the value of the targeted investments we have made in our grid over the past decade,” said ComEd President and CEO Gil Quiniones. “Our proposed grid plan charts a path for continuing to deliver nation-leading reliability, while keeping affordability top of mind, even in a future with more extreme weather events and unprecedented growth in power demand. We believe that reliability should not come at the expense of affordability, and we are working hard to keep customer bills as low as possible."

The recognition comes as northern Illinois faces new pressures on its power grid. Families and businesses are using more electricity than ever as homes, vehicles and buildings go electric, and severe storms are becoming more frequent and intense. That’s why ComEd’s Grid Plan which will be decided upon in December, is designed to protect the reliability customers count on today and prepare the grid for the decades ahead.

“Congratulations to ComEd on this national recognition, reinforcing Illinois’ nation-leading position in electric reliability,” said Governor JB Pritzker. “As energy demands continue to grow, we remain focused on strengthening our electric grid, lowering costs for working families and businesses, and building a cleaner, more reliable energy future for all Illinoisans.”

Since ComEd began its smart grid investments in 2012, those upgrades have helped customers avoid nearly 27 million power interruptions and more than $5 billion in outage-related costs. Overall reliability, measured by how long customers are without power, has improved by more than 75 percent compared with the 2007–2011 average. Outages lasting 12 hours or more have fallen 69 percent over the same period. These investments include smart switches that automatically reroute power, stronger poles and wires, modernized substations and better storm preparedness. Together, they have also sped up recovery after severe weather. In 2025, ComEd restored power to half of customers affected by storms within two hours and 98 percent within 24 hours. Had it not been for grid investments, an additional 2.6 million customers would have lost power.

“Reliable energy infrastructure is essential to Illinois’ ability to attract investment, support businesses, and create jobs,” said Illinois Economic Development Corporation President and CEO Christy George. “ComEd is an important partner in that work, and this national recognition underscores the strength of our state’s energy infrastructure."

A recent study by ComEd and Argonne National Laboratories projects that the number of heavy rainfall events, as well as more instances of severe weather, in northern Illinois, defined as those producing more than two inches of precipitation, could nearly double by mid-century. To prepare, ComEd is already bringing more durable technologies to the grid like fibreglass poles and elevated substations, developing management strategies to address severe storms, warmer temperatures, invasive pests and tree health risks that can affect vegetation near power lines and planning for new environmental threats that could affect utility equipment and infrastructure.

Severe weather data helps inform grid investments, including ComEd’s latest multiyear grid plan, filed in January, that builds upon its previous plan to strengthen the grid, continue delivering safe and affordable electric service as well as nation-leading reliability for ComEd’s customers amid the challenges of increasingly extreme weather and rising energy demands. The plan aligns with the state’s clean energy and economic development growth goals reflected in the Illinois Climate and Equitable Jobs Act (CEJA) and the Clean and Reliable Grid Affordability Act (CRGA).

Grid Flexibility Award

ComEd also received the ReliabilityOne® Grid Flexibility Award which is presented to a ReliabilityOne® recipient that demonstrated a dedicated focus on providing its customers and grid users with means to cost effectively use the grid to meet their needs. ComEd demonstrated the ability to interconnect a variety of distribution energy resources as well as the ability to monitor and control their outputs to maintain safe, reliable and resilient power throughout the year. These flexible interconnections have been used to defer system upgrades, helping customers get additional value from existing infrastructure investments and enabling clean energy to be added to the system as cost effectively as possible.

ComEd expects to connect approximately 400 community solar projects by the end of 2026 with a little over 320 interconnected year-to-date. Approximately 500 community solar sites are currently within ComEd’s construction interconnection queue, and more than 500 additional projects are currently in the study phase of interconnection to assess system impact. As of October, approximately 8 gigawatts (GW) of renewable generation are interconnected within the ComEd zone, including 6 GW of utility-scale renewable generation and 2 GW of distributed generation resources. Increasing the supply of solar on the grid is critical to meeting the rising energy demands of Illinois.

All utilities operating electric delivery systems in North America are eligible for consideration for the ReliabilityOne® Award. This year we recognize six leading utilities in their respective regions, which include utilities from the Northeast, Mid-Atlantic, Midwest, Upper Midwest, Southeast, and Pacific Regions. The selection of provisional recipients is based primarily on system reliability statistics that measure the frequency (SAIFI) and duration of customer outages (SAIDI and CAIDI). After provisional recipients are selected, each company undergoes a rigorous certification process which provides an independent review and confirmation of the policies, processes and systems used to collect, analyze and report a company's reliability results. Additional awards are recognized based on analysis of certification findings.

About ComEd

ComEd is a unit of Chicago-based Exelon Corporation (NASDAQ: EXC), a Fortune 200 company and one of the nation’s largest utility companies, serving more than 10.7 million electricity and natural gas customers. ComEd powers the lives of more than 4 million customers across northern Illinois, or 70 percent of the state's population. For more information visit ComEd.com, and connect with the company on Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, X, and YouTube.

PA Consulting believes in the power of ingenuity to build a positive human future. As strategies, technologies and innovation collide, we create opportunity from complexity. Our diverse teams combine deep expertise, innovative thinking and breakthrough technologies to help clients adapt, transform and achieve enduring results across consumer and manufacturing, defense and security, energy and utilities, financial services, government and public services, health and life sciences, and transport. As a Jacobs company, we combine strategic advisory, design and delivery as a single partner across the full program lifecycle. Together, our global team of approximately 47,000 help clients shape investment decisions, solve complex challenges and deliver lasting outcomes. Discover more at paconsulting.com and connect with PA on LinkedIn and X. PA. Bringing Ingenuity to Life.

PA Consulting’s ReliabilityOne® study is based on standard industry reliability statistics that measure the frequency and duration of electric power outages. As a group, customers of ReliabilityOne® participants on average experienced over 56% fewer sustained outages, and their collective system saw 64% shorter outage durations than the average US investor-owned utility. Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Valkea Resources Corp. (TSXV: OZ) (OTCQB: OZBKF) (FSE: 4A7) (the "Company" or "Valkea") has today published its quarterly financial statements and Management Discussion and Analysis. Both documents are available on the Company's website and SEDAR+. Valkea is also pleased provide an update on its exploration activities in northern Finland, including preliminary metallurgical results from its Aarnivalkea West prospect. Systematic exploration of 24 new high-ranking prospects (see July 22, 2026, press release) has commenced with reconnaissance base of till ("BoT") drilling underway and systematic diamond drilling ("DDH") drilling of the most prospective targets at the Paana Project set to recommence in early January

Highlights

  • Cash of C$9.6 million at the end of September 2026
  • Positive metallurgical test work results received indicate mineralisation at Aarnivalkea West is non-refractory, with high gold leach recoveries
  • Reconnaissance base of till ("BoT") drilling ongoing
  • Diamond drilling to commence at Paana in first week of January focussed on new targets highlighted by new BoT drilling.

Thomas Credland, CEO of Valkea Resources, said: "We continue to build a critical mass of new drill-ready targets ahead of the recommencement of diamond drilling in early January 2027, with the onset of winter conditions. Improved targeting has resulted from the acquisition and geological interpretation of new high-resolution UAV-magnetic surveys from two licence areas. These are being ground-truthed by a systematic BoT sampling program. Furthermore, we are encouraged by the results of diagnostic metallurgical test work from the advanced Aarnivalkea West prospect, which shows potential for non-refractory mineralisation at Paana."

Drilling at Paana

New geochemical data from Valkea's ongoing BoT drilling is being received and interpreted to provide further focussing and prioritisation of drill targets across the wider Paana licences. Planning for the BoT campaign was based on a new geological interpretation identifying 12 prospects on the wider Paana project (Figure 1) and has subsequently been refined by a high-resolution UAV-magnetic survey, flown in September.

Drilling of Kari, our first new target, was completed in August. Kari was prioritised due to its all-season access and BoT anomalism from a historic survey. The initial program of 1,275 m was drilled in five holes along an E-W profile, located 2.5 km south of known mineralisation at Aarnivalkea West. Although drilling returned evidence of disseminated sulphide mineralisation within the more deformed host lithologies in three out of five drillholes, no significant gold mineralisation was assayed. The work highlighted the unreliability of historic BoT datasets, justifying Valkea's emphasis on generating a critical mass of new more reliable BoT geochemical data to support targeting on the recommencement of diamond drilling in early January 2027.

Metallurgical test work results for Aarnivalkea West

Exploratory metallurgical test work undertaken by Alfred H Knight (UK) on a ~60 kg composite sample from Aarnivalkea West, with an assayed grade of around 1.0 g/t Au, showed mineralisation to be non-refractory in nature. Whole ore leach testing produced high extractions between 93.5% to 96% (95% at a grind size of 106 microns). In addition, batch flotation test work completed for rougher grind sizes, between 75-150 microns, also yielded high recoveries between ~93 and 96%. The test material has Bond Ball Mill Index of 10.8 kWh/t, classifying it as soft to medium hardness.

About Valkea

Valkea Resources is a geoscience-led exploration company focused on making new gold and base metal discoveries in Northern Finland's Central Lapland Greenstone Belt. Its 350 km2 land package includes six principal project areas that span highly prospective regional geological structures. The Company's leadership and technical team include key contributors to the multi-million-ounce Ikkari gold discovery, made in 2020. Work is underway to make a new discovery using the same systematic and disciplined approach to identifying mineral targets with the best potential for the possibility of becoming mines of the future.

New Ships, Expanded Destinations and Enhanced Guest Experiences Shape Carnival's Next Chapter

NEW YORK, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Carnival Cruise Line President Christine Duffy today announced plans for two new ships that will introduce a new class to the Carnival fleet. To be built by long-time partner Fincantieri and delivered in 2033 and 2035, the approximately 130,000-gross-ton LNG-powered ships are intentionally designed on a smaller scale, enabling access to more ports and expanding destination and itinerary choices.

"With a 29-ship fleet, we know our guests appreciate choices," said Duffy. "They love the incredible experiences and amenities on our Excel Class ships, the largest in our fleet, but they also love the intimacy our smaller ships offer. This new class gives us the best of both worlds, helping future-proof our fleet with the flexibility to take America's Cruise Line to even more places in the years ahead."

Duffy also shared a first look at Carnival Destiny, major expansions at Celebration Key, Grand Bahama, enhancements at RelaxAway, Half Moon Cay and plans to extend popular onboard benefits ashore. With more than 6.5 million guests sailing each year, Carnival has a unique perspective on what guests want from their vacations and is putting that feedback at the center of what comes next.

"Guests are seeking more choice, more flexibility and more ways to make the most of their time together," said Duffy. "What we are announcing today reflects how we're making Carnival cruise vacations even more personal, connected and fun."

Carnival Destiny Delivers More Choice with More Sea to See

Carnival Destiny, debuting in 2029 and the first of three Ace Class ships, is designed to give guests more ways to shape their cruise vacation around what they enjoy most. Built around its promise of More Sea to See, the ship will bring guests closer to the ocean with more outdoor space, expansive views and venues that make the sea part of the experience. Highlights include:

  • More outdoor pools than any other Carnival ship, including the first outward-facing main pool zone. Throughout the ship there will be eight pools, including six infinity pools, totaling more than 11,200 square feet of water surface,

  • An expansive ocean-front lanai that features several pools and brings dining and bar venues closer to the sea,

  • New premium venues with sweeping multideck ocean views, including a new exclusive pool on Deck 18 Aft, a total of 25 new dining and bar experiences, as well as a reimagined Limelight Lounge.

Carnival Destiny will dedicate nearly twice the space to family venues and attractions compared with Carnival's newest ships, bringing a family zone with mini golf, arcades, dining and other family favorites together in one area. It will also introduce Dr. Seuss Splash Station, a new splash pad inspired by The Cat in the Hat and Thing One and Thing Two, featuring water cannons and a dedicated area for children in swim diapers. The new attraction builds on Carnival's 13-year partnership with Dr. Seuss Enterprises and expands its popular Seuss at Sea programming.

Adults will have more choices of their own, with Carnival Destiny introducing Carnival's first adult-only zone spanning four decks. The zone will feature Carnival's first adult-only staterooms, an expanded Serenity adult-only retreat and an exclusive rooftop pool deck.

More Choice Ashore: The Next Evolution of Paradise Collection

Duffy also shared that Carnival is expanding the choices available ashore with the next evolution of Paradise Collection by Carnival, the largest portfolio of exclusive destinations across The Bahamas, Caribbean and Mexico.

The collection includes six distinct destinations: Celebration Key in Grand Bahama; RelaxAway, Half Moon Cay; Isla Tropicale in Roatan; Amber Cove in the Dominican Republic; Puerta Maya in Cozumel and Grand Turk in Turks & Caicos.

Building on the early success of Celebration Key, which has welcomed more than 3.25 million guests since its opening in July 2025, Carnival revealed plans for two new expansion phases for the destination that will increase total land-side capacity by 6,000 guests, with 3,000 added in each phase.

In 2028, a new portal will introduce even more ways for guests to play and relax together with a heated, beach-entry pool with a swim-up bar; a new social waterslide designed for four to five guests to slide together; and a colorful, aqua play area featuring five waterslides, a dry climbing play structure and drenching bucket created especially for younger children.

In 2030, a new major water park will add 18 waterslides, the cruise industry's longest lazy river with float-up bars and swim-in/swim-out cabanas, as well as a new exclusive area with an infinity pool, more beach access and new dining and bar concepts.

Carnival also announced Serenity Beach, a new complimentary retreat for guests 21 and older coming to RelaxAway, Half Moon Cay in spring 2027. It will feature dedicated loungers and bar and beverage service, with daybeds and cabanas available for an additional charge.

Greater Value from Ship to Shore

Beginning in February 2027, Carnival will extend its drink packages CHEERS!, CHEERS! Zero Proof™, Bottomless Bubbles™ and CHEERS! Social to Celebration Key and RelaxAway, Half Moon Cay, giving guests who purchase these Carnival packages greater value for their vacation dollars.

For additional information on Carnival Cruise Line and to book a cruise vacation on Carnival, call 1-800-CARNIVAL, visit http://carnival.com or contact your favorite travel advisor or online travel site.

ABOUT CARNIVAL CRUISE LINE

Carnival Cruise Line, part of Carnival Corporation (NYSE: CCL), the world's largest cruise company with a portfolio of cruise lines operating in over 800 ports & destinations worldwide – and is proud to be known as America's Cruise Line and for carrying more Americans and serving more U.S. homeports than any other. Carnival sails more than six and a half million guests annually and in 2023 was the first cruise line to sail more than 100 million guests in total. Operating from 13 U.S. and four Australian homeports, as well as seasonally from Europe, Carnival hosts more than 95,000 guests on its ships every day of the year and employs more than 50,000 team members, representing 120 nationalities.

Since its founding in 1972, Carnival has continually revolutionized the cruise industry and popularized the cruise vacation as an affordable and fun travel option. Carnival's fleet of 29 ships reflects an exciting period of growth that continues with the addition of seven ships through 2035: a fourth and fifth Excel class ship scheduled for 2027 and 2028, respectively; three Ace class ships scheduled for delivery in 2029, 2031 and 2033, beginning with Carnival Destiny; and two additional ships in the new class expected to be delivered in 2033 and 2035. Carnival's newest guest offering is its all-new exclusive destination, Celebration Key on Grand Bahama, which debuted in 2025 to join the company's Paradise Collection of Caribbean gems.

OLD GREENWICH, Conn.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Ellington Credit Company (NYSE: EARN) ("we") today reported financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Highlights

  • Net asset value (NAV) per share was $4.04 as of September 30, 2026, which includes the effects of distributions of $0.24 per share for the quarter.
  • GAAP net income was $3.7 million, or $0.09 per share.
  • Net investment income ("NII") was $6.7 million, or $0.17 per share.
    • Adjusted net investment income1 was $6.7 million, or $0.17 per share.
  • CLO portfolio was $332.0 million as of September 30, 2026.
    • CLO debt investments—$146.4 million
    • CLO equity investments—$185.6 million
    • Purchased $41.5 million of CLO investments and sold $31.5 million, across 61 trades.
  • Weighted average GAAP yield2 for the quarter, based on amortized cost, was 12.9% on the total CLO portfolio.
  • Received $14.5 million in recurring cash distributions3 from the CLO portfolio, or $0.37 per share.
  • Raised net proceeds of $5.5 million through the issuance of approximately 1.27 million common shares at prices representing a 3% weighted average premium to NAV per share.
  • Subsequent to quarter end, reset our monthly distribution rate to $0.05 per share, effective with the distribution payable in January 2027.

Management Commentary

“Ellington Credit generated an economic return of 2.4% for the third calendar quarter, or 9.9% annualized, as our active trading and disciplined risk management helped us navigate renewed market volatility,” said Laurence Penn, Chief Executive Officer and President. “Our CLO mezzanine debt and equity portfolios both contributed positively, led by net investment income. Our credit hedges generated gains for the quarter and helped protect NAV per share as credit spreads widened in September. These positive contributions were partially offset by losses on interest rate hedges associated with our fixed-rate unsecured notes. We are proud to have continued our relative outperformance, generating positive GAAP earnings in a challenging quarter when the vast majority of our peers reported losses.

“We remained highly active during the quarter, executing 61 distinct CLO trades and continuing to rotate capital toward investments where we see more attractive risk-adjusted returns. Our overall portfolio size was roughly unchanged quarter over quarter, as sales, paydowns and deal calls largely offset new investment activity. Importantly, the weighted average yield on assets acquired during the quarter increased to 16.7%, up from 14.9% in the second quarter.

“Adjusted net investment income increased by $0.02 sequentially to $0.17 per share, and we continue to see opportunities for further increases through additional capital deployment, selective use of leverage, and continued portfolio rotation. Our Board of Trustees has reset our monthly distribution rate to $0.05 per share, or $0.15 per quarter, a level supported by our current NII. We believe that this positions us to maintain an attractive, sustainable distribution that is well covered by net investment income, while also building NAV per share.”

CLO Performance

During the quarter ended September 30, 2026, the Morningstar LSTA U.S. Leveraged Loan Index generated a total return of 1.9%, despite persistent credit dispersion and renewed volatility toward quarter end. Returns were supported by investor demand for floating-rate assets, a recovery in certain discounted loans, particularly in the software sector, and refinancings and maturity extensions. Double-B- and single-B-rated loans generated positive returns over the quarter, while triple-C-rated loans underperformed as rising interest rates pressured highly leveraged borrowers, particularly in cable and telecommunications. Loan prices declined in late September amid heightened inflation concerns and broader market volatility.

The European leveraged loan market underperformed the U.S. market, with more pronounced weakness in lower-quality credits. Headwinds included uncertainty over France’s fiscal and political outlook, energy-price volatility, and some forced selling from European credit funds.

CLO performance was mixed, as constructive loan-market technicals were tempered by the late-quarter selloff. Within CLO mezzanine debt, shorter-spread-duration, more seasoned positions benefited from stronger performance in shorter-maturity loans and principal paydowns that reduced deal-level leverage and strengthened structural credit protections. Meanwhile, higher-quality CLO equity positions with longer reinvestment periods benefited from stronger-than-anticipated interest payments in July, while limited loan repricing activity continued to support excess spread and equity cash flows.

However, higher borrowing costs pressured highly leveraged borrowers, weighing on CLO investments — particularly European CLO equity and lower-rated debt positions — with greater exposure to lower-quality collateral. In September, CLO tranche spreads widened modestly, and CLO equity valuations came under renewed pressure as broader markets weakened.

Our CLO mezzanine debt and equity portfolios each generated positive results for the quarter, as net investment income more than offset net realized and unrealized losses in our CLO equity investments. Credit hedges generated gains for the quarter overall, including in September, helping cushion the impact of that month’s spread widening on NAV per share. Additional headwinds included losses on interest rate hedges associated with our unsecured notes, and mark-to-market losses on the notes themselves as credit spread tightening more than offset the impact of higher interest rates.

We executed 61 distinct CLO trades during the quarter, with sales and paydowns largely offsetting new investment activity. The weighted average yield on assets acquired during the quarter increased to 16.7%, compared with 14.9% in the second quarter. At September 30, 2026, our CLO portfolio had a fair value of $332.0 million and a weighted average projected yield of 18.3% based on fair value.

Key Terms

collateralized loan obligationsfinancial
A collateralized loan obligation is a financial product that pools many corporate loans and repackages them into slices sold to investors, with some slices offering steady, lower returns and others offering higher returns but more risk. Like splitting a pizza into pieces for different tastes, CLOs let investors pick their preferred risk level and help banks fund lending, so changes in CLO performance influence credit availability and can move markets.
net asset valuefinancial
Net asset value is the total value of an investment fund's assets minus any liabilities, divided by the number of shares or units outstanding. It represents the per-share worth of the fund, similar to how the value of a house is determined by its total worth after debts are subtracted. Investors use it to gauge the true value of their holdings and to compare different investment options.
View in glossary
non-GAAP financial measurefinancial
A non-GAAP financial measure is a way companies present their financial results that excludes certain expenses or income to show how they believe their core business is performing. It matters because it can give a clearer picture of how the company is really doing, but it can also be used to make results look better than they actually are.
total return swapsfinancial
A total return swap is a contract where one party agrees to pay another the full economic performance—price changes plus income—of an asset, while the other party pays a regular fee or interest. Think of it like renting the gains and losses of a stock or bond without owning it: investors can gain exposure, hedge positions, or add leverage more cheaply, but they take on the risk that the counterparty might fail to honor payments and that synthetic holdings can affect leverage and transparency.
